sections.heading: EPDM Roofing vs. TPO for Commercial Properties: Downsides and Energy Efficiency

runs.v: is known for exceptional durability and weather resistance: the synthetic rubber stretches and recovers through freeze-thaw cycles, keeps its flexibility across wide temperature ranges, handles thermal expansion and contraction well, and has been used on flat roofs for decades. It comes in thicknesses from 45 mil to 90 mil and offers economical installation and low lifecycle maintenance costs, which makes it cost-effective for commercial buildings. The downsides of EPDM roofing are heat absorption, seams, and punctures: black EPDM absorbs heat while white EPDM reflects solar heat, so energy efficiency trails reflective TPO, which reduces cooling costs, unless white EPDM or a coating is used; splice seams need experienced technicians; and foot traffic around equipment can puncture the membrane. Delivering exceptional results on either membrane comes down to seams, flashings, and drainage, so choose contractors who specialize in commercial flat roofing and have the expertise to protect the building, its siding, and its gutters. Newark Quality Roofing installs EPDM, TPO, and modified bitumen, so a reliable team can match the materials to the building.

faqs.q: How long does EPDM roofing last on a Montclair commercial building?

runs.v: EPDM rubber membrane lasts 15 to 25 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, against TPO at 7 to 20 years and modified bitumen at 20 years, and seam separation is the failure mode that usually ends its service.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial EPDM roof in Montclair, NJ?

runs.v: Yes, once roof work on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building exceeds 25% of the roof area in 12 months, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7; that is the 25% rule. The Rehabilitation Subcode requires complete removal of a water-soaked covering or a roof with 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4, so confirm the permit path with the Montclair construction office.

faqs.q: Does an EPDM roof on a Montclair historic-district building need extra approval?

runs.v: It can, mainly when the work changes the building's appearance; properties in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the Montclair construction office before work. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: Should you choose EPDM over TPO for a Montclair low-slope roof?

runs.v: EPDM records 15 to 25 years and TPO 7 to 20 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart; EPDM fails most often at the splice seams and TPO at the welded seams, per NRCA technical guidance, so the choice follows the building, its rooftop equipment, and the Essex County climate.

runs.v: EPDM commercial roofing in New Jersey runs about $7.00 to $10.00 per square foot installed, per published NJ contractor pricing, with flat-roof repair at $2.50 to $10.00 per square foot, per HomeGuide cost data. Final cost depends on roof size, slope, membrane, and access.

faqs.q: What are the common problems with EPDM roofs?

runs.v: Seam separation, membrane shrinkage at edges and penetrations, ponding water, punctures, and aging flashings cause most EPDM leaks, which is why a Newark Quality Roofing inspection starts at the seams and drains.
